evidence: Cic. Sen. 19: cujus ā morte tertius hic et trīcēsimus annus est
terms.comment: Of a time or a time of life: ā puerō, ā parvulō, since childhood; stronger, jam inde ā. What has lasted until now takes the present tense with jam: jam dūdum animus est in patinīs, my mind has been on the dishes for ages.

evidence: Liv. 26.19.5: ex quō togam virīlem sūmpsit
terms.comment: ex eō tempore, since then; ex quō, since the time when.

phrases.latin: Ēdūxī ā parvulō; habuī, amāvī prō meō
phrases.english: I brought him up from when he was tiny; I kept him and loved him as my own

phrases.latin: nam mihi magna cum eō jam inde ūsque ā pueritiā fuit semper familiāritās
phrases.english: for he and I have always been close friends, ever since we were boys

phrases.latin: cujus ā morte tertius hic et trīcēsimus annus est
phrases.english: this is the thirty-third year since his death

phrases.latin: ex quō togam virīlem sūmpsit nūllō diē prius ūllam pūblicam prīvātamque rem ēgit quam in Capitōlium īret
phrases.english: from the day he came of age, he never did any business, public or private, without first going up to the Capitol

phrases.latin: Jam dūdum animus est in patinīs.
phrases.english: My mind has been on the dishes for ages.

sources: Lewis & Short: ab · Lewis & Short: ex · Lewis & Short: jam
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-livius, loci-terentius), checked against the editions named there.
Terence (Parry’s text) and Cicero, De senectute checked against the Perseus Latin texts (11 November 2026).
In Cic. Sen. 19 Lewis & Short prints quintus; the Perseus text, followed here, has tertius.
